origin.description: Create a URI with the data: scheme by encoding the payload in base64 or with URI percent-encoding.

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: Raw vector, connection, or character vector to use as payload. Character vectors of more than one element are collapsed with a newline before encoding.

arguments.name: mime
arguments.text: MIME type of the data. An empty string omits the type from the URI and is interpreted as text/plain;charset=US-ASCII per the standard.

arguments.name: encoding
arguments.text: Either "base64" or NULL for URI encoding.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: File name to open as the payload. file and data are mutually exclusive.

origin.value: A string of the form data:[mime][;base64],<encoded-payload>.

translation.description: Build a data: URI from bytes, a text or binary connection, or strings that are collapsed like R character data.

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: Bytes, a file object, or strings or numbers that are collapsed when they are not raw. Omit when file is set.

arguments.name: mime
arguments.text: MIME type string. An empty string leaves the type out of the prefix.

arguments.name: encoding
arguments.text: The string "base64" or None for percent-encoding of raw bytes.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: Path read in binary mode. Cannot be combined with data.

translation.details: Only raw payload bytes are encoded. Collapsed text from connections or character data raises the same error as R when encoding is requested.
translation.example:
from base64enc.dataURI import dataURI
x = bytes(range(1, 11))
print(dataURI(x))
print(dataURI(x, encoding=None))
